### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f41a424c8f36baaab1b27db770c8a4ce843e83b8` — the merge of head `cc250df8a0f36a33c470d073ffcaaa716f5b2118` into base `5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f41a424c8f36baaab1b27db770c8a4ce843e83b8 && git checkout f41a424c8f36baaab1b27db770c8a4ce843e83b8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613 cc250df8a0f36a33c470d073ffcaaa716f5b2118 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613 && git merge --no-ff cc250df8a0f36a33c470d073ffcaaa716f5b2118

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613
```

</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cc250df8a0f36a33c470d073ffcaaa716f5b2118`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/email-config.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/capability-arg.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-email-base-url-parity.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts

Inputs read: card #29485 (body and all three comments: triage, Claim, os-dev-report), PR #29539 (body, 3-file list, net diff against `main` at the head above), and the 65 check-runs on the head. Read-only: the cited code was read on a local clone at a recent `origin/main` (`390bd2ae`) that contains both the PR base `5651647d` and the #29478 landing commit `73c24394e2`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set — unchanged, right.** `defaultTemplateContext` stays `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()` on `EmailServiceConfigSchema`; `StackEmailConfigSchema` inherits it through `.omit({ apiKey, options })`, so nothing an author can write is newly accepted or refused on either schema. The card's "⛔ No schema change" holds.
- **Public surface — a `.describe()` string and a TSDoc block, right.** `packages/spec` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts` as source, so both publish; `/meta/types` and the generated reference carry the new describe. The describe carries no tracker number (`check:doc-authoring` shape holds); `#5448`, `PR #5498` and `#29095` sit in TSDoc only, in the file's existing citation style.
- **Generated output — right.** `content/docs/references/system/email-config.mdx` changes exactly two rows (the service schema and the inherited stack row), matching the two schemas that carry the key. A grep of the PR head finds no residue of the old wording ("except appName, which", "One key is not passed through") anywhere in the tree: no test pinned it, and no other generated artifact embeds it.
- **Gates — all green.** On the head, the ten required contexts are `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI is `skipped` by its own path filter with Type Check UI / Test UI / Build & E2E UI / Live E2E UI `success`); all sixteen Test UI shards completed `success`. Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards and Spec property liveness are `success`. No governed path is in the file list.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29485-email-template-baseurl-describe.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` — right. The diff publishes text only (a describe string and a docblock in a shipped source file), no shape, no type, no default. `Clause-②: no` is on both the PR body and the changeset, consistent with each other and with a diff that neither widens nor narrows what the spec accepts. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: `email` config is operator config, not a metadata type.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` — nothing to answer. The five declared deviations, each judged:

1. Model-free trailer pair on both commits (`Claude-Session` + `Co-authored-by: Claude`) instead of the harness's model-named line — read off `git log`; this is what AGENTS.md and the pre-push hook require. Accepted.
2. Branch `claude/project-thread-5qav58`, not `claude/issue-29485-*` — recorded in the Claim comment as the card-thread platform exception; the PR body carries `Fixes #29485`, so discoverability is through the card. Accepted.
3. PR assignee / reviewer requests skipped per the dispatch order — no effect on the contract. Accepted.
4. Human Minimum 3 left unticked (`pnpm lint` not run locally) — `Lint · ESLint` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on the head. Accepted.
5. WIP push before the spec build — the head carries both commits and the generated row matches the source. Accepted.

Out-of-scope note (not filed by the dev): the file-top docblock still says "`appName` is the one key whose env layer is not `OS_EMAIL_*`". Judged against the schema: that sentence enumerates the schema's own keys (`provider`, `apiKey`, `defaultFrom`, `retries`, `persist`, `queueDelivery`, `options`, `appName`, `defaultTemplateContext`), and `baseUrl` is a member of the `defaultTemplateContext` record, not a key of the schema, so it stays true. Not escalated; the card's wanted list scoped the edit to the `defaultTemplateContext` docblock and describe.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/email-config.zod.ts` — judged against the ruling it implements (card #29485, which carries ruling A on #29095 barring the spec edit from that card and handing the text to the spec lane) and its first consumer (`resolveEmailCapabilityArg` in `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/capability-arg.ts`, the single reader of `config.email`). Every new sentence about live behaviour, tried against the tree:

- "`OS_AUTH_URL` (legacy `BETTER_AUTH_URL`) → `OS_BASE_URL` → this map's `baseUrl` → `http://localhost:` plus the serve port" — true, in that order: `resolveDeploymentBaseUrl` reads `env.OS_AUTH_URL ?? env.BETTER_AUTH_URL ?? env.OS_BASE_URL ?? cfgEmail.defaultTemplateContext?.baseUrl ?? \`http://localhost:${port}\``.
- "the serve port (`OS_PORT`, legacy `PORT`, else `3000`)" — true: `const port = env.OS_PORT ?? env.PORT ?? '3000'` in the resolver, and `serve.ts`'s `--port` default is `readEnvWithDeprecation('OS_PORT', 'PORT') ?? '3000'`; the parity test pins both orders (`OS_PORT over PORT`, `legacy PORT when OS_PORT unset`).
- "with any trailing slash trimmed" — true: `.replace(/\/+$/, '')` on the resolved value, and the parity test's `OS_BASE_URL: 'https://base.example.com/'` case expects the slash gone.
- "Both are always present in the delivered context" — true: the resolver builds `{ ...cfgTemplateContext, appName: resolveDeploymentAppName(...), baseUrl: resolveDeploymentBaseUrl(...) }`, so both keys are set on every boot; `email-plugin.ts` passes `this.options.defaultTemplateContext` to the service unchanged.
- "A send's own `data` still wins over both, as it does over every key here" — true: `EmailService.sendTemplate` builds `{ ...(this.options.defaultTemplateContext || {}), ...(input.data || {}) }`, the per-call data spread last.
- "Writing it here is the fallback for a deployment that sets neither env var" — true: it is the fourth operand, after the three env reads and before the localhost tail. (Nuance, not a finding: `??` means a set-but-empty env var is a value and does not fall through to the config rung, as the resolver's own docblock records; the spec text says "env first" and does not claim otherwise.)
- "`baseUrl` follows the same order (#29095)" — env wins, as for `appName`; the citation is right. `73c24394e2` is `feat(plugin-email): every email template can read the deployment address as {{baseUrl}} (#29478)` with `Fixes #29095` in its body, and it is an ancestor of `main`, so the card's premise ("lands after PR #29478 merges") is satisfied.
- The describe's short clause ("baseUrl takes OS_AUTH_URL, then OS_BASE_URL, then the value written here, then the local http://localhost default, with no trailing slash") is the card's wanted shape — env first, the written value, the local default, no trailing slash — and matches the chain; it omits the legacy `BETTER_AUTH_URL` alias and the port, which the TSDoc above it carries. Acceptable brevity for a one-clause describe, and it introduces no `{{…}}` (the docs generator's brace trap the `appName` describe already notes).
- The `appName` chain restated in the new bullet is unchanged and still matches `resolveDeploymentAppName` (`OS_APP_NAME || cfgEmail.appName || defaultTemplateContext.appName || configAppName || 'ObjectStack'`).

Pre-existing, re-wrapped by the hunk but not new: "the CLI passes this object through to `EmailServicePlugin` as written". On main the reader is `resolveEmailCapabilityArg` in `@objectstack/plugin-email`, invoked through `@objectstack/core`'s `capability-composition` by both `os serve` and `bootStack`; "the CLI" is the historical phrasing the file-top docblock already corrects. Outside the card's wanted list; not a finding.

Findings: none must-fix, none should-fix.

> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
